title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 59-69 of this file). E and E' are sets with a symmetric relation x|o|y. Reading |o| as 'disjoint' or 'orthogonal' is my interpretation. For A ⊂ E, A|o|B means every element of A is related to every element of B.

The operator written 's-pr°' here (supp° on the neighbouring pages) is defined by
  B ⊂ supp°_E(A) ⟺ ∀x ∈ E, (x|o|A ⇒ x|o|B).
So supp°_E(A) = A^{⊥⊥}, the double-orthogonal (Galois) closure, and Σ_E is the set of closed subsets.

A correspondence α : E → P(E') induces ᾱ(A) = ⋃_{x∈A} α(x) and α_*(S) := supp°_{E'}(ᾱ(S)).

Problem left open on the previous page. The formula α_*(supp°_E A) = supp°_{E'}(ᾱ A) holds in the direction ⊇. The remaining question is ⊆, i.e. whether ᾱ is 'continuous' for the two closure operators: ᾱ(A^{⊥⊥}) ⊂ (ᾱA)^{⊥⊥}. Equivalently: if B ⊂ A^{⊥⊥}, is ᾱ(B) ⊂ ᾱ(A)^{⊥⊥}?

Step 1: a sufficient condition. Suppose there is an adjoint correspondence β : E' → P(E) with
  (*) x|o|β(x') ⟺ α(x)|o|x'.
Taking unions gives
  (**) A|o|β̄(B') ⟺ ᾱ(A)|o|B'.

Step 2: the implication follows. By (**) and symmetry, x'|o|ᾱ(A) ⟺ β(x')|o|A. This implies β(x')|o|B because B ⊂ A^{⊥⊥}. By (**) again, β(x')|o|B ⟺ x'|o|ᾱ(B). Grothendieck flags in the margin that symmetry of |o| was used.

Step 3: the optimal adjoint. Put γ(x') = {x ∈ E | α(x)|o|x'}, which depends on α alone. Then (*) says exactly that γ(x') = β(x')^⊥, written co-supp°(β(x')).

Step 4 (finished on p.66). β exists iff each γ(x') is closed, i.e. γ(x') ∈ Σ_E. The largest such β is β(x') = γ(x')^⊥.

This is the theory of adjointable maps between orthogonality spaces, i.e. Galois-connection-preserving morphisms of a symmetric polarity. Grothendieck is heading toward a proposition about a category of 'disjonctions' with correspondences as morphisms (the crossed-out draft on p.66). The adjointable correspondences presumably induce maps Σ_E → Σ_{E'} that preserve the closure lattice.
errors: No mathematical error. The argument is correct, given the symmetry of |o| that Grothendieck explicitly notes he used.
The question 'is β optimal?' (marked '?') is settled on the next page: existence iff γ(x') ∈ Σ_E, and the largest β is β(x') = γ(x')^⊥.
Minor: the page leaves open whether adjointness is also necessary for the inclusion. It is only shown to be sufficient.

ideas.what: Double-orthogonal closure supp°(A) = A^{⊥⊥} on a set with a symmetric 'disjointness' relation; Σ_E is the lattice of closed sets
ideas.modern_name: Galois closure of a symmetric polarity / orthogonality space (Dacey space); complete ortholattice of orthoclosed sets

ideas.what: Adjoint correspondence β with x ⊥ β(x') ⟺ α(x) ⊥ x', used to prove that ᾱ is continuous for the ⊥⊥-closures
ideas.modern_name: Adjointable maps between orthogonality spaces; Chu-space morphisms (adjointness condition r(a, g(b')) = s(f(a), b')); Galois-connection morphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Foulis (Baer *-semigroups, 1960); Barr (Chu construction, 1979); Pratt; Paseka–Vetterlein (orthogonality spaces, 2010s)

ideas.what: Canonical maximal adjoint β(x') = γ(x')^⊥ with γ(x') = {x : α(x) ⊥ x'}; it exists iff γ(x') is orthoclosed
ideas.modern_name: Existence criterion for the adjoint of a map of orthogonality spaces (preimage of an orthoclosed set is orthoclosed)

missed.claim: In 1986, in an unclear context, Grothendieck appears to have rediscovered, independently, the notion of adjointable morphisms between orthogonality spaces ('disjonctions'). This is essentially the Chu / Foulis–Randall framework, including the criterion for when an optimal adjoint exists. The material is standard elsewhere; the only new item would be the historical fact.
missed.quote: Pour l'affirmer, il faudrait une corr. en sens inverse β : E' → P(E) telles que l'on ait ... x|o|β(x') ⟺ α(x)|o|x'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical interest only: it documents Grothendieck working on orthogonality-space or Chu-like structures. The mathematics itself is not new.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but elementary Galois-connection reasoning, matching well-known notions (adjointable maps of orthogonality spaces, Chu morphisms). The only mildly interesting point is that Grothendieck reinvents this framework in 1986.
transcription_corrections: The top page number reads '65' (Grothendieck's own numbering), while the archive page number is 68. The machine-transcribed 'previous page' header '68' is probably the archive number of page 64.
's-pr°' is very likely the same symbol written 'supp°' on the neighbouring pages (support/closure operator), abbreviated as 's~pp°'.
'ou encore dans ce cas' is probably 'ou encore, dans ces cas' / 'ou encore ceci'.
'Si encore, il n'y a telles corr. β existe' should read approximately 'Si une telle corr. β existe, il doit y en avoir une optimale'.
The margin reads 'On a utilisé x|o|y ⇒ y|o|x !'.
